newsitem.title: USA: Transamerica consumer unit posts Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Transamerica consumer unit posts Q3 loss.

text.p: Transamerica Corp on Thursday said its consumer lending business posted a loss in the third quarter, reflecting Transamerica's decision to increase loan loss reserves and restructure its operation.
Transamerica's consumer lending operations reported a loss of $65.7 million in the third quarter, compared to income of $24.2 million a year earlier.

The consumer lending loss pushed the overall loss for the finance division, which includes consumer lending, commercial lending and leasing, to $25.2 million for the quarter, versus a profit of $56.1 million a year ago.

During the 1996 quarter, Transamerica decided to segregate and liquidate a portfolio of about $1.1 billion of its receivables, consisting of non-real estate loans and certain inadequately performing real estate secured loans.

As a consequence, the company increased its loan loss reserves so that at September 30, its allowance for losses for the above portfolio was 11.3 percent of receivables, and the allowance for the core portfolio, which totals $3.5 billion in receivables, was 4.7 percent of receivables.
Total delinquent receivables were $176.3 million, or 3.72 percent of finance receivables outstanding at September 30, 1996, compared to $147.3 million, or 3.02 percent, at June 30, 1996.
Going forward, the insurance and financial services company said it will emphasize its home equity real estate secured lending.

As reported, overall net income, including investment transactions and special items, for the third quarter of 1996 was $1.67 per share, or $113.9 million, down 20 percent from net income of $2.08 per share, or $147.0 million, in the 1995 period.

Third-quarter 1996 net income included $0.01 per share in investment losses and $0.01 per share from special items, while year-earlier net income included $0.36 per share of investment gains and $0.17 per share of special items.

Transamerica's life insurance operations reported record operating income, excluding investment gains, in the 1996 third quarter of $84.1 million, up seven percent from $78.6 million in the 1995 third quarter, which included $7.3 million of special benefits.
The real estate unit earned $16.6 million, up from $12.1 million a year ago.

"Our life insurance and leasing businesses turned in record performances and most of our other businesses performed well this quarter," said Frank Herringer, Transamerica chairman and chief executive officer. "In addition, we were pleased with the favorable resolution of certain tax matters. The loss in our consumer lending business resulted from our decision to significantly increase loan loss reserves and our intent to restructure the consumer lending operations."
